titulo: Present subjunctive (forms): Irregulars: the yo form, stem changes and the six rebels

aula.objetivo: Form the present subjunctive of regular verbs, of irregular verbs from the «yo» form («tenga», «haga», «diga»), of stem-changing verbs and of the six verbs with their own forms («sea», «esté», «vaya», «haya», «sepa», «dé»), with the spelling changes (busque, llegue, empiece).

sessao.titulo: Irregulars: the yo form, stem changes and the six rebels

blocos.titulo: Irregular verbs: the «yo» rule and the six rebels
blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: the «yo» rule works for most irregular verbs. If the «yo» form of the present is irregular, the subjunctive carries that irregularity into every person: tengo → tenga, tengas, tenga, tengamos, tengáis, tengan; hago → haga; digo → diga; vengo → venga; pongo → ponga; salgo → salga; traigo → traiga; oigo → oiga; veo → vea; conozco → conozca; conduzco → conduzca; caigo → caiga. STEP 2: stem-changing verbs (e → ie, o → ue) change in «yo, tú, él, ellos», but NOT in «nosotros» or «vosotros» — the same "boot" pattern as the present: pensar → piense, pienses, piense, pensemos, penséis, piensen; poder → pueda, puedas, pueda, podamos, podáis, puedan; querer → quiera, quieras, quiera, queramos, queráis, quieran. STEP 3: -ir verbs with a stem change ALSO change in «nosotros» and «vosotros»: dormir → duerma, duermas, duerma, durmamos, durmáis, duerman; sentir → sienta, sientas, sienta, sintamos, sintáis, sientan; pedir → pida, pidas, pida, pidamos, pidáis, pidan. STEP 4: six verbs have their own forms and are worth memorising (their «yo» doesn't end in «-o»: soy, estoy, voy, he, sé, doy): ser → sea; estar → esté; ir → vaya; haber → haya; saber → sepa; dar → dé. STEP 5: «esté» has an accent in every form except «estemos»: esté, estés, esté, estemos, estéis, estén. «Dé» has an accent only in the «yo» and «él» forms, to tell it apart from the preposition «de»: dé, des, dé, demos, deis, den. STEP 6: -uir verbs add «y» before the vowel: construir → construya, construyas…; «leer» is regular: lea, leas… STEP 7: a practical tip: when you meet a new verb, first ask yourself "what's the «yo» form?".
blocos.comparacao: The six rebels are exactly the verbs whose «yo» doesn't end in «-o» (soy, estoy, voy, he, sé, doy): sea, esté, vaya, haya, sepa, dé. For everything else, the «yo» form is your key: «tengo → tenga», «hago → haga», «digo → diga». English has nothing like this, so learn the six as a set.

tabelas.titulo: The six verbs with their own forms

erros.motivo: The subjunctive inherits the «yo» form (tengo → tenga) and uses the ending «-as».
In -ar and -er verbs, «nosotros» and «vosotros» keep the original stem.
In -ir verbs with a stem change, «nosotros» and «vosotros» use «u» (dormir) or «i» (sentir, pedir).
Only «dé» (yo and él) has an accent; «des» doesn't.

blocos.enunciado: Say out loud the subjunctive of tener, hacer, ir, ser, estar and saber for «tú» and «nosotros». Then say five sentences starting with «Quiero que tú…» using these verbs. These are just the forms for now; don't worry about the exact meaning.
Say out loud the subjunctive of hablar, comer and vivir for «yo», «nosotros» and «ellos». Check yourself against the table.
